questions.question: The equation of a line passing through the point (2, -3) and perpendicular to the line x + 2y = 4 is

questions.explanation: First, find the slope of the given line x + 2y = 4. Convert to slope-intercept form: 2y = -x + 4 y = (-1/2)x + 2 The slope of this line (m1) is -1/2. Since the required line is perpendicular to this line, its slope (m2) will be the negative reciprocal of m1. m2 = -1 / m1 = -1 / (-1/2) = 2. Now, we have the slope (m = 2) and a point (2, -3) through which the line passes. Use the point-slope form: y - y1 = m(x - x1). y - (-3) = 2(x - 2) y + 3 = 2x - 4 Rearrange to standard form: 2x - y = 3 + 4 2x - y = 7

questions.question: An architect is designing a cable-stayed bridge. One of the main support cables can be modeled as a straight line. The cable starts from a point A(2, 5) on the bridge deck and reaches a pylon at a point B(x, y). Another supporting cable is designed to be perpendicular to the first cable and passes through the point C(6, 1). The equation of this second cable is found to be y = (1/2)x - 2. Based on the information, what is the slope of the first main support cable (passing through A and B)

options.explanation: Incorrect slope value for the first cable, this is the slope of the second cable
Incorrect slope value for the first cable
Correct slope value for the first cable after finding the slope of the second cable and using the relationship for perpendicular lines
Incorrect slope value for the first cable

questions.explanation: The second supporting cable has the equation y = (1/2)x - 2. From this equation, its slope (m2) is 1/2. The first main support cable is perpendicular to this second cable. If two lines are perpendicular, the product of their slopes is -1 (m1 * m2 = -1). Let m1 be the slope of the first main support cable. m1 * (1/2) = -1 m1 = -1 / (1/2) m1 = -2 So, the slope of the first main support cable is -2
